title: Capstone: Config File Parser
description:
```
; settings.ini
[window]
width = 1280
title = "My Game"
fullscreen = false

[audio]
volume = 0.8
```

```
window.width      = 1280 (int)
window.title      = My Game (string)
audio.volume      = 0.8 (double)
audio.music       : missing, using 0.5
window.width as bool: TypeError "1280" is not true or false
```
hints: Parse line by line: trim it; skip it if empty or a comment; `[name]` sets the current section; otherwise split at the first `=`, trim both sides and remove surrounding quotes from the value.

Inside `get<T>`: `if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, int>) return std::stoi(text); else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<T, bool>) { ... }`. Only the branch for `T` is compiled (lesson 9.03). `std::is_same_v<A, B>` (from `<type_traits>`, explained in lesson 11.02) is simply `true` when `A` and `B` are the same type.
`std::stoi` throws `std::invalid_argument` on text that is not a number: catch it inside `get` and throw your own `TypeError` with the key in the message.
requirements: Parse sections, `key = value` lines, quoted strings and comments starting with `;` or `#`
Values are stored as text under `"section.key"`, for example in a `std::vector` of `{ key, value }` structs (in milestone 10 a `std::map` does this job better)
Read the settings text line by line with `std::getline(std::cin, line)`; reading it from a real file comes in lesson 10.06
`template <typename T> T get(const std::string& key) const` for `int`, `double`, `bool` and `std::string`, using `if constexpr`
Errors as exception classes derived from `std::runtime_error`: `ParseError` (with the line number), `MissingKeyError`, `TypeError`
stretch: Lists (`a, b, c` as `std::vector<T>`), `set<T>` and saving the file back out.
